title: Structured Identity v1 Milestone 1 design inspection

claims.statement: Across 380 outer-train/outer-test nuisance summaries, conditioning on preceding_identity, omission_position, sequence_family, and cycle gives max P(expected_identity | nuisance combination) = 1.0 for every summary; all 380 conditioning-key sets are deterministic.

The persisted outer-fold table contains 294 folds; 14 have only one training cycle, 3 have no A trials in training, and 3 have no B trials in training. Inner metadata emits 14 insufficient_training_groups records.

On the explicit contract smoke tensor with shape (4, 3, 5), R1 vectorization reshapes back to the identical R2 samples: R0=(4,3), R1=(4,15), R2=(4,3,5). This is a contract check only; real neural feature tensors were not materialized.

issues: The current omission ontology makes preceding_identity a deterministic relabeling of expected_identity within omission position; a decoder can therefore succeed on the nuisance target while appearing to decode expected identity.
Several outer folds cannot support the planned nested model-selection contract without an explicit fold/cell exclusion rule.
No model was trained and no neural feature tensor was materialized in this review.

verification.verdict: training_gate_remains_closed; resolve nuisance non-identifiability and fold geometry before Milestone 2

falsifier: This review is superseded by a versioned specification amendment or a new design receipt demonstrating an explicitly justified estimand in which expected identity is not deterministically recoverable from the declared nuisance variables and all training folds satisfy the nested-validation contract.
